Rashi on Ketubot 51a:10:1.english: He is not permitted - For he already became obligated for her redemption once she was taken captive.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:10:2.english: [He is] obligated to heal her - For healing is like sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:10:3.english: [He is] permitted - For a man is not obligated to sustain his divorcee.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:11:1.hebrew: פלוגתא דרבי מאיר ורבי יהודה - בפרק אע"פ:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:11:1.english: The dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah - [It is] in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:12:1.hebrew: והיא כותבת התקבלתי כו' - לשון שובר, ואפי' לא נתקבלה. ולר' מאיר אינה יכולה למחול בעודה תחתיו, ומתני' נמי, דקתני לא כתב לה כתובה גובה כתובתה שלימה, קא סלקא דעתך ואפילו מחלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:12:1.english: And she writes: "I have received," etc. - [This is] the wording of a receipt, even [if] she did not receive [it]. And according to Rabbi Meir, she cannot waive [her ketubah] while she is [married] to him. And our Mishnah as well, which teaches, "[If] he did not write a ketubah for her, she collects her full ketubah," it enters your mind [that she collects it] even [if] she waived [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:13:1.hebrew: אחראין לכתובתיך חייב - שנשתעבדו נכסיו, וקס"ד נשתעבדו בכל דין שעבוד כאילו נכתב בתוך השטר, ואם ימכור נכסיו תטרוף לקוחות:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:13:1.english: [A] guarantee for your marriage contract, he is obligated - [meaning] that his property became liened, and we initially assumed [that] it became liened with every law of a lien, as if it were written inside the document, and if he sells his property, she may seize [it from the] buyers.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:13:2.hebrew: אתאן לר' יהודה - דאמר שטר שלא נכתב בו אחריות, לא מדעת המלוה נעשה, אלא סופר טעה, והרי הוא כמי שנכתב, וטורף מן המשועבדים:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:13:2.english: We come to Rabbi Yehuda - Who said [that] a document in which a guarantee was not written was not made [that way] with the lender's consent; rather, the scribe erred, and it is as though it were written, and [the lender] collects from encumbered [property].

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:2:1.hebrew: יתום ויתומה - אח ואחות, ונכסיהם ביד אפוטרופוס:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:2:1.english: An orphan boy and an orphan girl - A brother and a sister, and their property [was] in the hand of a guardian.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:2:2.english: Increase [the allowance] for the orphan boy on account of the orphan girl - Increase extra sustenance for the orphan boy so that his sister will be sustained with him.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:3:1.english: Where there are two - [She is] his sister, and she will serve him.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:4:2.english: [The court] removes [it] for the daughters from the sons - For sustenance and for dowry.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:4:3.hebrew: ולבנות מן הבנות - לקטנות מן הגדולות; אם אין שם אלא בנות והחזיקו גדולות בנכסים, מוציאין מידם וחולקות בשוה. והכא ליכא מזוני, שאין הבנות נזונות מן הבנות, לפי שכולן שוות בירושה:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:4:3.english: And for the daughters from the daughters - [This refers] to the younger [daughters] from the older [daughters]; if there are only daughters there and the older [daughters] took possession of the property, [the court] removes [it] from their possession and they divide [it] equally. And here there is no [question of] sustenance, for daughters are not sustained from [other] daughters, since they are all equal in inheritance.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:4:4.english: And for the sons from the sons - For the younger [sons] from the older [sons], to divide equally.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:5:1.hebrew: אבל לא לבנים מן הבנות בנכסים מועטין - שאין בהן כדי לזון אלו ואלו עד שיבגרו, דאמרי רבנן: הבנות יזונו והבנים ישאלו על הפתחים:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:5:1.english: However, not to the sons from the daughters in [a case of] a small [amount of] property - Where there is not enough in [the property] to sustain both these and those until they reach majority, for the Rabbis said: The daughters shall be sustained, and the sons shall go begging at the doors.

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:8:1.hebrew: ולא כתב לה כל נכסים כו' - חייב להיות כל הנכסים אחראין לה, ולא יכול לומר לה: אין ליך אלא שדה הכתובה לך בשטר כתובתיך:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:8:1.english: And he did not write for her: All property, etc. - [He is] obligated for all [his] property to serve as a guarantee for her, and he cannot say to her: "You have only the field that is written for you in your ketubah document."

Rashi on Ketubot 51a:9:1.hebrew: ובכהנת - שאינו יכול לקיימה משנשבית, כותב לה: "אפרקינך ואהדרינך למדינתך", לפי שאשת כהן אסורה לבעלה אם נאנסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 51a:9:1.english: And in [the case of] a priestess - Since he cannot keep her [as his wife] once she has been taken captive, he writes for her, "I will redeem you and return you to your province," because the wife of a priest is forbidden to her husband if she was violated.

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:10:1.hebrew: אמר הרי גיטה וכתובתה תרפא עצמה רשאי - לפי שרפואה היא בכלל מזונות, והרי קבלה כנגד מעשה ידיה שעד עכשיו; אבל אינו רשאי לומר "תקבל את גיטה ותפדה את עצמה", לפי שלא קבלה תשלום מפירות שאכל עד עכשיו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:10:1.english: [If] he said: "Here is her bill of divorce and [the payment of] her marriage contract, let her heal herself," he is permitted [to do so] - Because healing is included in [the obligation of] sustenance, and she has already received [sustenance] in exchange for her handiwork up until now; however, he is not permitted to say, "Let her receive her bill of divorce and redeem herself," because she has not received compensation for the usufruct [of her property] that he consumed up until now.

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:11:1.hebrew: מני ר' מאיר היא דאמר כל הפוחת כו' - בפרק אע"פ (לקמן כתובות דף נו:) דייק: "כל הפוחת" — אפי' בתנאי; אלמא סבר דתנאו בטל ואית לה, וכיון דאמר לית לה לא סמכה דעתה, והוי בעילתו בעילת זנות. ופריב"ן דבכל מקום דאית לה ואין האשה בטוחה בו דלא סמכה דעתה — תקנו חכמים שיהא בעילתו בעילת זנות; אבל אם היה תנאו קיים, כיון דלית לה, אין בעילתו בעילת זנות. ואלמנה, אע"פ דבדרבנן תנאו קיים, הכא תנאו בטל, דכל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון. וקשה לר"י: דבפרק החובל (ב"ק דף פט. ושם) משמע דאפי' היכא דלית לה הוי לר' מאיר בעילת זנות, משום שלא תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה. דפריך התם הש"ס גבי אשה שחבלה בבעלה לא הפסידה כתובתה: ואמאי? תזבין לכתובתה בטובת הנאה לבעלה כו'! ומשני: הא מני? ר"מ היא, דאמר: אסור לאדם שישהא עם אשתו שעה אחת בלא כתובה; מ"ט? שלא תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה. על כן נראה דר"מ "לא מבעיא" קאמר: לא מבעיא היכא דלית לה דהויא בעילתו בעילת זנות משום דקלה בעיניו להוציאה, אלא אפילו אית לה, כיון דלא סמכה דעתה, הויא בעילתו בעילת זנות. ודייק מדלא קתני "כל בתולה שאין לה מאתים ואלמנה שאין לה מנה הרי היא בעילת זנות", אלא נקט "כל הפוחת" — משמע שבא לומר אע"ג דתנאו בטל ואית לה, הויא בעילת זנות. וקשה לר"י: דמנא לן ד"כל הפוחת" ואפי' בתנאי? דלמא בתנאי מודה ר"מ דתנאו קיים, ד"כל הפוחת" — דמשמע דאפילו באותו ענין שיש לה — היינו בסוף ביאה, דאמרינן בפ' אע"פ (לקמן כתובות דף נז.) דאינה מוחלת? וי"ל: דלשון "כל הפוחת" משמע שהוא פוחת לה, ובסוף ביאה אינו יכול לפחות לה, אלא היא פוחתת לעצמה, ולא שייך לשון פחת אלא בתנאה; א"נ, מדנקט "כל" קא דייק. וא"ת: דבפרק אע"פ (שם) אמר דבסוף ביאה לדברי הכל אינה מוחלת, ובהחובל (ב"ק פט. ושם) משמע שיכולה למכור ולמחול? ויש לומר כדפירש הקונטרס לקמן: דדוקא בעל פה אינה מוחלת, דאמירתה לאו כלום היא כיון דכבר זכתה, אלא אם כן כתבה שובר. ואם תאמר: ומאי קאמר "הא מני רבי מאיר היא"? הא משמע בפרק אע"פ (לקמן שם) דלרבי יהודה נמי אינה יכולה למחול דתנאו בטל, ודווקא בכותבת לו "התקבלתי" קאמר? ויש לומר: דהתם מיירי לפי המסקנא דשמעתין, דקאמר "ואי בעית אימא רבי יהודה", התם בכתבה ליה "התקבלתי". ואם תאמר: ומנא לן דלרבי מאיר אפילו בכתבה ליה "התקבלתי" לא מצי מחלה, דקאמר "מני ר' מאיר היא"? דלמא ר"מ לא מבעיא ב"התקבלתי" קאמר דמצי מחלה דהויא בעילת זנות, אלא אפי' בעל פה דתנאו בטל הויא בעילת זנות? וי"ל: דהשתא אין נראה לו לחלק בין כתבה ללא כתבה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:11:1.english: Who is [the author]? It is Rabbi Meir, who said: "Anyone who decreases, etc." - In the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (later in Ketubot 56b), [the Gemara] infers: "Anyone who decreases" — even by stipulation; thus he holds that his stipulation is void and she has [the full ketubah], and since he said [to her] that she does not have [it], her mind is not at ease, and his intercourse is licentious intercourse. And Rivan explained that in any case where she has [the ketubah] and the woman is not confident of it, such that her mind is not at ease, the Sages enacted that his intercourse should be licentious intercourse; however, if his stipulation were valid, since she does not have [a ketubah], his intercourse would not be licentious intercourse. And [regarding] a widow, even though in a rabbinic [obligation] one's stipulation is valid, here his stipulation is void, because whatever the Sages enacted, they enacted along the lines of Torah law. And Ri found this difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 89a and there [in the commentary]), it is implied that even where she does not have [a ketubah], according to Rabbi Meir it is licentious intercourse, so that she will not be light in his eyes to divorce her. For the Talmud asks there regarding a woman who injured her husband [that] she did not forfeit her ketubah: "Why? Let her sell her ketubah for a small benefit to her husband, etc.!" And it answers: "Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Meir, who said: It is forbidden for a man to remain with his wife for a single hour without a ketubah. What is the reason? So that she will not be light in his eyes to divorce her." Therefore, it appears that Rabbi Meir is speaking in the "not only" style: not only where she does not have [a ketubah] is his intercourse licentious intercourse, because she is light in his eyes to divorce her, but even [where] she has [it], since her mind is not at ease, his intercourse is licentious intercourse. And [the Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that it does not teach, "Any virgin who does not have two hundred [dinars] or widow who does not have a maneh, behold this is licentious intercourse," but rather states "Anyone who decreases" — implying that it comes to say [that] even though his stipulation is void and she has [it], it is licentious intercourse. And Ri found this difficult: from where do we know that "Anyone who decreases" [means] even by stipulation? Perhaps regarding a stipulation Rabbi Meir agrees that his stipulation is valid, and "Anyone who decreases" — which implies even in a situation where she has [the ketubah] — refers to the end of intercourse, where we say in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (later in Ketubot 57a) that she cannot waive [it]? And one can answer: that the wording "Anyone who decreases" implies that he decreases [it] for her, whereas at the end of intercourse he cannot decrease [it] for her, rather she decreases [it] for herself; and the language of "decreasing" only applies to a stipulation. Alternatively, from the fact that he stated "Anyone," [the Gemara] makes this inference. And if you ask: in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (ibid.), it says that at the end of intercourse, according to all opinions, she cannot waive [it], whereas in HaChovel (Bava Kamma 89a and there), it is implied that she can sell and waive [it]? One can answer as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained later: that specifically orally she cannot waive [it], because her statement is nothing since she has already acquired [it], unless she wrote a receipt. And if you ask: what does [the Gemara in HaChovel] mean by saying, "Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Meir"? Behold, it is implied in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (later, ibid.) that according to Rabbi Yehudah as well she cannot waive [it], because his stipulation is void, and he only spoke [of where she can waive it] when she writes to him, "I have received [my ketubah]"? One can answer: that there [in Af Al Pi] it speaks according to the conclusion of our sugya, which says, "And if you wish, say it is Rabbi Yehudah," there [meaning] when she wrote to him, "I have received [my ketubah]." And if you ask: and from where do we know that according to Rabbi Meir, even when she wrote to him, "I have received [my ketubah]," she cannot waive [it], such that [the Gemara] says, "Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Meir"? Perhaps Rabbi Meir is speaking in the "not only" style: not only regarding "I have received," where she can waive [it], is it licentious intercourse, but even orally, where his stipulation is void, it is licentious intercourse? And one can answer: that now it does not appear [right] to him to distinguish between [where] she wrote [a receipt] and [where] she did not write [one].

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:11:2.hebrew: מני רבי מאיר היא - השתא משמע ליה מתני' דלא כתב לה, היינו לפי שהתנה עמה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:11:2.english: Who is [the author]? It is Rabbi Meir - At this point, [the Gemara] understands [the case in] the Mishnah where he did not write [a ketubah] for her [to mean] that this is because he stipulated with her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:13:1.hebrew: אתאן לר' יהודה דאמר אחריות טעות סופר הוא, רישא ר"מ, סיפא ר' יהודה - אסיפא בלא רישא ה"מ לדקדק: מני? אי רבי מאיר — הא אמר אחריות לאו טעות סופר הוא; אי רבי יהודה — כתב לה שדה שוה מנה במאתים, אמאי חייב? והא לרבי יהודה יכולה למחול! אלא דרך הש"ס דמדקדק מרישא כל כמה דמצי למידק. וכענין זה יש בפרק כירה (שבת לט:) גבי מעשה שעשו אנשי טבריא, ובפרק קמא דעירובין (דף טז.) גבי "נמצאת שלשה מדות במחיצה". [וע"ע תוספות שבת לט: ד"ה אלא פניו וכו', ומש"ש על הגליון]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:13:1.english: We come to Rabbi Yehuda, who said [omission of] a guarantee is a scribal error; the first clause is Rabbi Meir, [and] the latter clause is Rabbi Yehuda - [The Gemara] could have raised the question of whose [opinion the Mishnah reflects] from the latter clause [alone] without [needing] the first clause: if [it is] Rabbi Meir — behold, he said [omission of] a guarantee is not a scribal error; [and] if [it is] Rabbi Yehuda — [when] he wrote for her a field worth a maneh for two hundred [zuz], why is he obligated? Surely according to Rabbi Yehuda she is able to waive [part of her marriage contract]! Rather, it is the way of the Talmud to raise its question from the first clause as much as it is able to. And similar to this is found in chapter Keirah (Shabbat 39b) regarding the incident that the people of Tiberias did, and in the first chapter of Eruvin (16a) regarding "three rules were found concerning a partition." [And see further Tosafot on Shabbat 39b, s.v. Ella panav, etc., and what is written there in the margin.]

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:1:1.hebrew: סוף סוף כל העומד לגזוז כגזוז דמי – אע"ג דפלוגתא דר"מ ורבנן היא בפרק שבועת הדיינין (שבועות מג. ושם) בענבים העומדים ליבצר — דר"מ סבר כבצורות דמיין ורבנן סברי לאו כבצורות דמיין — מ"מ פריך הכא בפשיטות דכגזוז דמי, כמו שפר"ח דמההיא דפרק הכונס (ב"ק דף נט: ושם) קיימא לן הכי; דקאמר התם: "רבי שמעון אומר: אכלה פירות גמורין — משלמת פירות גמורין, אם סאה סאה, אם סאתים סאתים", דחשבינן להו כתלושים, ופסקינן התם הלכה כר"ש. אבל אין לומר דבהנהו דאי קיימי מכחשי מודו כ"ע דכבצורות דמיין, דבהשולח (גיטין דף לט.) ובפרק קמא דסנהדרין (דף טו.) משמע דבהא נמי פליגי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:1:1.english: Ultimately, anything that is about to be sheared is considered sheared - Even though this is a dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis in the chapter Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 43a, and there [in the parallel discussions]) regarding grapes that are about to be harvested — for Rabbi Meir holds they are considered as harvested, while the Rabbis hold they are not considered as harvested — nevertheless, [Abaye] raises the objection here as a matter of course that it is considered sheared, as Rabbeinu Chananel explained, that from that [Mishnah] in the chapter HaKones (Bava Kamma 59b, and there) we hold this way; for it states there: "Rabbi Shimon says: If [an animal] ate fully ripe produce, [the owner] pays [for] fully ripe produce — if a se'ah, a se'ah; if two se'ah, two se'ah," for we regard them as detached, and we rule there that the halakhah follows Rabbi Shimon. However, one cannot say that regarding those [fruits] which, if they remain [attached], would deteriorate, everyone agrees that they are considered as harvested, for in [the chapter] HaShole'ach (Gittin 39a) and in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15a) it is implied that in this [case] as well they disagree.

Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:2:1.hebrew: ממקרקעי ולא ממטלטלי בין למזונות בין לפרנסה - וא"ת: קשיא דרבא אדרבא! דבפרק מציאת האשה (לקמן כתובות דף סח.) פסיק רבא הלכה כר"י, דאמר: ינתן לשניה כדרך שנתן לראשונה; ואמרינן התם דשמואל כר"י ס"ל. אלמא סבר רבא דשמין באב, וא"כ גביא ממטלטלי, כדאמרינן בשמעתין! וליכא למימר דהתם רבא משמיה דרב חסדא קאמר לה, וליה לא ס"ל; דהא התם בההיא סוגיא פריך מינה אמילתיה דרבא גופיה, ולא קא משני הכי! וי"ל: דהא דאמר רבא הכא "ממקרקעי ולא ממטלטלי" — היינו בדלא אמידניה; והא דסבר רבא התם כרבי יהודה ושמואל — בדאמידניה, שדעתו שתגבה ממטלטלי. וכה"ג מפליג הש"ס התם. ונראה דבזמן הזה, דכולהו גבי ממטלטלי — כתובה ומזונות מתקנת הגאונים, ופרנסה נמי אנן סהדי שכל בני אדם רגילים להשיא בנותיהם ממטלטלי — וחשיב כמו באמידניה, דפסיק רבא כר"י:
Tosafot on Ketubot 51a:2:1.english: "From land but not from movable property, whether for sustenance, or whether for dowry" - And if you ask: [This statement of] Rava contradicts [another statement of] Rava! For in the chapter [entitled] Metziat HaIshah (below, Ketubot 68a), Rava rules that the halakhah follows R. Yehudah, who says: "[It] is given to the second [daughter] in the same manner as it was given to the first," and we say there that Shmuel holds like R. Yehudah. Thus, Rava holds that we assess the father's [disposition], and if so, she collects [her dowry] even from movable property, as we say in our sugya. And one cannot say that there Rava stated it in the name of Rav Chisda, while he himself does not hold [that view], because there in that sugya [the Gemara] raises an objection from it against Rava's own statement and does not answer in that way. One can answer: That which Rava says here, "from land and not from movable property," refers to where we have not assessed him; whereas that which Rava holds there like R. Yehudah and Shmuel refers to where we have assessed him [and determined] that his intent is that she collect from movable property. And in a similar vein, the Talmud distinguishes there. And it appears that nowadays, when all of them are collected from movable property — the marriage contract and sustenance by an enactment of the Geonim, and [as for] dowry as well, it is common knowledge that all people are accustomed to marry off their daughters using movable property — it is therefore considered as if we had assessed him, where Rava rules like R. Yehudah.
